domain: Political Economy / Institutional Theory / Market Design
topic_summary: Analysis of the naturalization of free markets as default institutional arrangement. Examines whether market dominance represents lapsed-alternative naturalization (engineered closure that has naturalized over time) or beneficiary-maintained naturalization (active post-hoc defense by incumbents). Tests D3 artifact shape hypothesis: whether current market arrangements are engineered-closure or lapsed-closure artifacts.

key_entities: State/regulatory apparatus (rule-setting authority for market operation)
Incumbent beneficiaries (actors whose position depends on current market structure)
Alternative coordination systems (commons management, gift economies, state planning)
Hayek/classical liberal tradition (intellectual framework naturalizing markets)
key_tensions: Markets as discovered vs designed (naturalization narrative vs historical construction)
Default status as inevitable vs actively maintained (lapsed vs beneficiary-maintained closure)
key_mechanisms: Intellectual naturalization (economic theory presenting markets as neutral/inevitable)
Legal enclosure (property rights systems foreclosing non-market coordination)
Path dependency (sunk costs and network effects making alternatives costly)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The legitimacy claim that free markets represent the natural, default state of economic coordination absent interference
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Economic orthodoxy and legal systems claiming authority to define what counts as 'natural' vs 'artificial' coordination

readings.commitment: Market dominance is a lapsed-closure artifact: active engineering that has naturalized over time, now defended through naturalization narrative rather than continued active maintenance
readings.authority_grounding: Historical institutionalism / path dependency / Polanyian embedded-economy frameworks
readings.expected_structural_delta: Enclosure mechanisms (property law, contract enforcement) identified as historical D3 artifacts whose origins are obscured; beneficiaries operate through naturalization narrative rather than active suppression; high victim set (those foreclosed from non-market coordination) but diffuse harm attribution

readings.commitment: Market dominance is actively maintained post-hoc by incumbent beneficiaries who defend it against alternatives through ongoing suppression and legal engineering
readings.authority_grounding: Critical political economy / regulatory capture frameworks / neo-Marxian state theory
readings.expected_structural_delta: Lobbying, regulatory capture, and legal barriers identified as active snare mechanisms; clear beneficiary set (capital holders, financial intermediaries); high victim set with concentrated harm attribution; ongoing extractiveness visible in current policy battles

readings.commitment: Markets emerge spontaneously from voluntary exchange and represent the baseline state absent coercive intervention; alternatives require active state engineering
readings.authority_grounding: Austrian economics / libertarian philosophy / spontaneous-order tradition
readings.expected_structural_delta: Property rights and contract enforcement seen as mountains (physical/coordination constraints); state interventions (regulation, taxation, planning) identified as ropes or snares imposing artificial constraints; victim set inverted (taxpayers, regulated firms)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Lapsed-alternative reading holds that all coordination systems (including markets) are constructed artifacts requiring active engineering; genuine-natural reading holds markets are the spontaneous default requiring no construction. No single framework can hold both that markets are constructed-then-naturalized and that they are pre-political spontaneous order.

Beneficiary-maintained reading identifies current market structure as actively imposed by powerful actors; genuine-natural reading identifies it as emerging from voluntary coordination. No single framework can hold both that market dominance requires ongoing coercive maintenance and that it represents absence of coercion.

axes.human_readable: Lapsed-Alternative Naturalization (Engineered Closure Naturalized Over Time)
axes.structural_delta: Market dominance as historical artifact of enclosure and legal engineering that has naturalized to the point where its constructed nature is obscured
axes.primary_observable: Historical enclosure timelines; legal property regimes vs pre-enclosure commons; naturalization narrative prevalence in economics discourse
axes.selection_reason: Core contested reading; D3 artifact hypothesis; lapsed-closure pattern test case

axes.human_readable: Beneficiary-Maintained Naturalization (Active Post-Hoc Defense by Incumbents)
axes.structural_delta: Market dominance as ongoing suppression of alternatives through regulatory capture, lobbying, and legal barriers actively maintained by current beneficiaries
axes.primary_observable: Lobbying expenditures by financial/corporate sectors; regulatory barriers to alternative coordination (co-ops, commons); legal suppression of mutual-aid systems
axes.selection_reason: Structurally distinct from lapsed-alternative (active vs lapsed maintenance); highest epsilon; tests engineered-closure hypothesis

axes.human_readable: Genuine Natural Default (Markets as Spontaneous Order)
axes.structural_delta: Markets as emergent baseline from voluntary exchange; state intervention as artificial constraint on natural coordination
axes.primary_observable: Transaction cost economics; spontaneous-order emergence in unregulated settings; regulatory burden measurements
axes.selection_reason: Counterfactual reading necessary for kernel structure; inverted victim set; tests whether baseline can be genuinely natural

axes.human_readable: Intellectual Naturalization Apparatus (Economic Theory as Legitimation)
axes.structural_delta: Economics profession's role in constructing and maintaining naturalization narrative through theory and pedagogy
axes.primary_observable: Econ curriculum treatment of markets vs alternatives; DSGE model assumptions; textbook framing
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: mechanism rather than structural reading; captured by naturalization narrative dimension within selected readings

axes.human_readable: Property Rights Enclosure (Legal Foreclosure of Commons)
axes.structural_delta: Property law as mechanism foreclosing non-market coordination by legally barring commons management and mutual aid
axes.primary_observable: Enclosure Act timelines; current legal barriers to community land trusts; co-op formation restrictions
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: historical mechanism component of lapsed-alternative reading; not independent axis

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Economics profession's role in constructing naturalization narrative
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Mechanism rather than independent reading; naturalization narrative captured within lapsed-alternative and beneficiary-maintained readings
Historical mechanism component of lapsed-alternative reading; not structurally independent

omegas.description: Do lapsed-alternative and beneficiary-maintained readings collapse empirically? If current beneficiaries are descendants of historical enclosure winners operating through naturalized institutions, the distinction between lapsed and active maintenance may be unstable.

Can any coordination system be 'natural'? If all require some degree of legal/social infrastructure, the genuine-natural reading may collapse into a question of which infrastructure is least visible or most taken-for-granted.
Who counts as foreclosed? Are gig workers victims of market naturalization (precarity) or beneficiaries (flexibility)? Boundary instability across readings.

Does analysis assume Western property/market history as universal baseline? Gift economies, rotating credit associations, and commons management in non-Western contexts may present alternative naturalization trajectories.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel structure validated: three readings hold genuinely different axioms about whether markets are constructed, naturally emergent, or actively maintained. Axiom contradictions declared between lapsed-alternative/genuine-natural and beneficiary-maintained/genuine-natural. Readings coexist socially (all three have live scholarly/political constituencies) but cannot be held simultaneously in a single coherent framework.
